title: Linear inequalities and number-line solutions
summary: Solve linear inequalities accurately, reverse the sign when required and represent endpoints and direction on a number line.
objectives: Solve one-step and multi-step linear inequalities.
Explain when and why the inequality sign reverses.
Draw open and closed endpoints and shade the correct direction on a number line.

blocks.text: Most steps used for equations also work for inequalities: simplify both sides, collect variable terms and isolate the variable. Addition and subtraction preserve order. Multiplication or division by a positive number also preserves order. The diagram shows the solution x ≤ 3 from the first worked example: a filled circle at 3 and shading to the left.

sections.title: Reverse when multiplying or dividing by a negative

blocks.text: If 2<5, multiplying by -1 gives -2>-5. The order reverses because points reflect across zero. Therefore dividing −3x > 12 by −3 produces x < −4. Write the reversed sign during the division step rather than trying to repair it later.

Use an open circle for < or > because the boundary is excluded. Use a filled circle for ≤ or ≥ because the boundary is included. Shade left for values smaller than the boundary and right for larger values. Test one shaded value in the original inequality to catch direction errors.

The most common error is forgetting to reverse the sign after dividing by a negative number. Others are using a filled circle for < or >, shading the wrong way, and writing 4 > x as x > 4 instead of x < 4. Testing one value from the shaded part catches all of these.

sections.title: Worked example: solve and draw

prompt.text: Solve 4x − 3 ≤ 9 and describe its number-line graph.

content.text: Divide both sides by 4, a positive number, so the sign stays the same.
Draw a filled circle at 3, because 3 is included, and shade to the left, as in the diagram.

sections.verification_note: The test value x = 0 gives −3 ≤ 9, which is true, so the shaded side is correct; x = 4 gives 13 ≤ 9, which is false.

sections.title: Worked example: handle a negative coefficient

content.text: Divide both sides by −2 and reverse the sign.

sections.verification_note: Testing x = −5 gives 7 + 10 = 17 > 15, which is true, while x = 0 gives 7 > 15, which is false.

prompt.text: For 2x-1<7, the solution is x<k. Find k.

feedback.text: Add 1 and divide by 2 to obtain x<4.

blocks.text: Solve an inequality like an equation, but reverse the sign whenever you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number.
On a number line, use an open circle for < or > and a filled circle for ≤ or ≥, shade towards the solutions, and test one shaded value in the original inequality.
